content.text: Energy is one of the most fundamental concepts in physics. Everything that happens involves energy changing from one form to another. Rather than thinking of "forms of energy," modern physics uses the concept of
—places where energy is held before being transferred elsewhere.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be transferred from one store to another. This is the principle of conservation of energy.
is the capacity to do work or cause change. It cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores or converted between types.
Energy can be stored in different ways

items.title: Kinetic
bullets: Examples: moving car, running person, spinning wheel

items.title: Gravitational Potential
items.description: Energy due to height in a gravitational field
bullets: Depends on mass, height, and gravitational field strength
Examples: object on a shelf, water behind a dam

items.title: Elastic Potential
items.description: Energy stored in stretched or compressed objects
bullets: Released when object returns to original shape
Examples: stretched spring, drawn bow, compressed ball

items.title: Thermal
items.description: Energy stored in hot objects (internal energy)
bullets: Examples: hot water, warm radiator, the Sun

items.title: Chemical
items.description: Energy stored in chemical bonds between atoms

items.title: Nuclear
bullets: Examples: uranium fuel rods, the Sun (fusion)

items.title: Electrostatic
items.description: Energy due to separated electric charges

items.title: Magnetic
bullets: Stored when magnetic poles are brought together or separated

content.text: Identify the main energy store in each situation: a) A car moving at 30 m/s b) A sandwich c) A rock at the top of a cliff d) A stretched catapult

a) Kinetic energy store (moving object) b) Chemical energy store (energy in food molecules) c) Gravitational potential energy store (height above ground) d) Elastic potential energy store (stretched material)
A ball is thrown upward. Describe the energy stores involved.
Energy transferred to thermal and sound
Describe the energy changes when a battery-powered toy car drives up a ramp.
Chemical energy store (battery) → Kinetic energy store (moving car) and Gravitational potential energy store (climbing ramp)
Some energy is also transferred to thermal energy store (friction, motor heating)
— Energy is never used up, only transferred to other stores (often thermal, which dissipates).
— Always specify the type: gravitational potential, elastic potential, or electrostatic potential.
— Light is an energy transfer mechanism (radiation), not a store.
— Heat is a transfer of energy, not a store. The store is thermal energy.
— Sound is a way of transferring energy (mechanical waves), not an energy store.

Light and sound are NOT energy stores. They are ways of transferring energy (radiation and mechanical waves respectively). The thermal energy store is the correct term for what was previously called 'heat energy'.

Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores

Energy transfers describe HOW energy moves between stores

At the highest point on one side, the pendulum has maximum GPE and zero KE (momentarily stationary). As it swings down, GPE decreases and KE increases. At the lowest point, GPE is at a minimum and KE is at a maximum. As it swings up to the other side, KE decreases and GPE increases until it is momentarily stationary again at maximum GPE.

Light and sound are not energy stores because they are mechanisms by which energy is transferred (pathways), not places where energy is held. Light is energy transferred by electromagnetic radiation, and sound is energy transferred by mechanical waves. Once the source stops, no energy remains stored in the light or sound itself.

Kinetic energy store (moving air) transfers energy by mechanical work to kinetic energy store (spinning turbine blades), then by electrical work via the generator to electrical energy, which is distributed to users. Some energy is transferred to thermal energy stores through friction in bearings and air resistance.
